sections.label: Scam cases and losses fall
sections.summary: Scam cases and losses fell in 2025 and continued falling in the first half of 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Senior Minister, Coordinating Minister for National Security and Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: After consecutive years of increases, both scam cases and losses fell in 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Senior Minister, Coordinating Minister for National Security and Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: This improvement continued into the first half of 2026, where reported scam cases fell by 14.4% to about 16,800 cases, while losses fell by 17.9% to about $411 million, compared to the same period last year.

sections.label: Bill advances anti-scam fight
sections.summary: The Bill advances the fight against scams through information exchange, legal levers on online platforms, and disrupting scam accounts.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Senior Minister, Coordinating Minister for National Security and Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: This is why addressing scams remains a top priority for the Government.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Senior Minister, Coordinating Minister for National Security and Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: This Bill advances our fight against scams in three ways: one, it supports information exchange between the Police and various service providers for scam disruption; second, it enhances the Government's legal levers to combat scams on online platforms; and third, it strengthens the Police's ability to disrupt the supply of scam accounts and conduct anti-scam operations.

sections.label: ADOs disable accounts
sections.summary: ADOs let the Police direct a service provider to disable an account suspected of use in a scam-related offence.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Senior Minister, Coordinating Minister for National Security and Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: ADOs will empower the Police to direct a service provider to disable an account, if the Police suspect or have reason to believe that the account has been or will be used preparatory to or in furtherance of a scam-related offence.

sections.label: ADO account disablement duration
sections.summary: Accounts may be disabled under ADOs for up to 30 days, with one possible extension of up to another 30 days.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Senior Minister, Coordinating Minister for National Security and Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Accounts may be disabled under ADOs for up to 30 days, with one possible extension of up to another 30 days.

sections.label: Penalties for Code non-compliance
sections.summary: For each non-compliance with the Code of Practice, the Competent Authority may impose a penalty of up to $10 million or issue a Rectification Notice.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Senior Minister, Coordinating Minister for National Security and Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Going forward, for each instance of non-compliance with the Code of Practice, the Competent Authority may impose a penalty of up to $10 million, or issue a Rectification Notice to rectify the non-compliance with the Code of Practice.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Senior Minister, Coordinating Minister for National Security and Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Where the non-compliance relates to an Implementation Directive, the Competent Authority may similarly impose a penalty of up to $10 million or issue a compliance order to the Implementation Directive.

sections.label: Maximum $10 million penalty
sections.summary: The maximum administrative financial penalty and fine for the Competent Authority and Courts is set at $10 million.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Senior Minister, Coordinating Minister for National Security and Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Second, we have set the maximum administrative financial penalty and fine that the Competent Authority and the Courts respectively can impose at $10 million.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Senior Minister, Coordinating Minister for National Security and Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: This maximum penalty will be the highest fixed quantum financial penalty in Singapore's statute book.

sections.label: OCHA directions by computer program
sections.summary: Clause 19 allows OCHA directions to be given by the operation of a computer program, including AI or machine learning technologies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Senior Minister, Coordinating Minister for National Security and Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The second key amendment to OCHA is in clause 19, which will allow OCHA directions to be given by the operation of a computer program, including those leveraging AI or machine learning technologies.

sections.label: Offences for misusing designated online accounts
sections.summary: Clause 16 creates offences for supplying designated online accounts or personal information, or consenting to such use, with knowledge or reasonable grounds to believe the account will be used unlawfully.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Senior Minister, Coordinating Minister for National Security and Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Clause 16 introduces new offences against those who misuse accounts from designated online services, to facilitate criminal activity.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Senior Minister, Coordinating Minister for National Security and Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: In particular, under the new sections 39GA and 39GC of the Miscellaneous Offences (Public Order and Nuisance) Act 1906 (or MOA), it will be an offence for a person to supply or offer to supply a designated online account to another person; or provide or offer to provide personal information to another person, or consent or offer to consent to personal information being used by another person for the purpose of opening a designated online account, if the person knew or had reasonable grounds to believe that the designated online account will be used for an unlawful purpose.

sections.label: Presumption of knowledge of unlawful purpose
sections.summary: A person is presumed to have known the designated online account will be used unlawfully if he supplied it or consented to personal information use for gain, or failed to take reasonable steps on identity, location or purpose.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Senior Minister, Coordinating Minister for National Security and Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: To address this, going forward, a person is presumed to have known that the designated online account will be used for an unlawful purpose in any of the following scenarios: one, the person supplied the designated online account or provided or consented to the use of his or her personal information for any gain; two, the person failed to take reasonable steps to ascertain the identity and the physical location of the person receiving the designated online account, or using the personal information to open a designated online account; or three, the person failed to take reasonable steps to find out the recipient's purpose for obtaining the designated online account, or using the personal information to open a designated online account.

sections.label: Penalties for designated online account offences
sections.summary: Individual offenders face a fine up to $10,000, imprisonment up to three years, or both, with higher penalties for repeat convictions and discretionary caning up to 12 strokes for scam-related knowledge or intent.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Senior Minister, Coordinating Minister for National Security and Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Offenders who are individuals will be liable for a fine not exceeding $10,000, or imprisonment not exceeding three years, or both.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Senior Minister, Coordinating Minister for National Security and Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: As for the offences under the new sections 39GA and 39GB regarding supplying designated online accounts, receiving designated online accounts and retaining control of designated online accounts opened using the personal information of others, the prescribed penalty for a second or subsequent conviction in respect of an individual person is a fine not exceeding $20,000, or imprisonment for a term not exceeding five years, or both.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Senior Minister, Coordinating Minister for National Security and Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: In addition, discretionary caning of not more than 12 strokes will apply where the individual knew or intended that the designated online account would be used to commit or facilitate any scam offence.

sections.label: SLOs restrict services up to three years
sections.summary: SLOs empower the Police to require service providers to restrict the provision of services to a person for up to three years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Senior Minister, Coordinating Minister for National Security and Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: SLOs empower the Police to require service providers to restrict the provision of services to a person for a period of up to three years.

sections.label: Officers obtain information for Restriction Orders
sections.summary: Clause 6 amends the Protection from Scams Act 2025 to empower specified officers to obtain information on persons who must be notified of a Restriction Order.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Senior Minister, Coordinating Minister for National Security and Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Second, clause 6 amends the Protection from Scams Act 2025 to empower specified officers, including Police Officers, Commercial Affairs Officers and CSOs, to obtain information on persons who must be notified of the issuance of a Restriction Order under the Protection from Scams Act.

sections.label: Daily scam reports and losses
sections.summary: The Police receives about 90 scam reports daily, with average daily losses of $2 million.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Senior Minister, Coordinating Minister for National Security and Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: At present, the Police has received an average of about 90 scam reports every day, with average daily losses amounting to $2 million.

sections.label: Online platforms and OCHA penalties
sections.summary: About 90% of scam cases in the first half of this year involved online platforms, and maximum penalties under the OCHA rise to S$10 million.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Senior Minister, Coordinating Minister for National Security and Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: In the first half of this year, about 90% of scam cases involved online platforms.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Senior Minister, Coordinating Minister for National Security and Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: For platforms that breach a Code of Practice or Implementation Directive under the OCHA, the maximum penalty for each instance of non-compliance will be raised to S$10 million.

sections.label: Police tools to act faster
sections.summary: The Bill gives the Police DOs, ADOs and SLOs to act faster against scam-linked accounts and digital services.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: They exploit gaps between systems and the Bill closes these gaps.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: It gives the Police practical tools to act faster: (a) the DO that compel banks, telcos and platforms to share information quickly when an account is suspected to be involved in scams; (b) ADOs that allow the Police to temporarily disable scam linked accounts for up to 30 days, extendable once; and (c) SLOs that limit access to digital services for individuals assessed to be enabling scams.

sections.label: Raised penalties for non-compliant platforms
sections.summary: Raising penalties from $1 million to $10 million compels platforms to invest in verification, warnings and faster takedowns.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: By raising penalties for non-compliant platforms from $1 million to $10 million, the Bill compels platforms to invest in better verification, clearer warnings and faster takedowns of scam content.

sections.label: Criminalising online account mule activity
sections.summary: The criminalisation of online account mule activity is a significant step.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The criminalisation of online account mule activity is a significant step.

sections.label: Automated real time alerts
sections.summary: A future step could be automated, real time alerts between banks, telcos and platforms when suspicious behaviour is detected.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: A future step could be automated, real time alerts between banks, telcos and platforms when suspicious behaviour is detected, without waiting for a formal order.

sections.label: Preventive friction and response times
sections.summary: The passage proposes tiered preventive friction and clear response time standards, noting the Bill raises penalties but does not specify response times.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: A tiered system of preventive friction, such as temporary limits or mandatory identity re-verification could prevent losses while investigations continue.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: This Bill increases penalties for non-compliance, but it does not yet specify response time standards.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Setting clear expectations, for example, requiring platforms to act within a defined number of hours within notification of scam content, could significantly reduce exposure time for victims.

sections.label: International anti-scam partnerships
sections.summary: The passage calls for collective domestic and international action, including global signal exchange, priority flagging and rapid takedown arrangements.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Scams and fraud must also be tackled collectively, both domestically and internationally, because the infrastructure of deception rarely respects national boundaries.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: I hope we continue to deepen partnerships with industry and overseas counterparts, including through global signal exchange, priority flagging and rapid takedown arrangements for phishing sites, impersonation accounts and other scam enablers.

sections.label: Scam statistics and crime share
sections.summary: The passage reports a 27.6% drop in scams and 17.92% decrease in losses in 2025, and that scams were about 60% of reported crimes from 2020 to mid-2025.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: SPF's 2025 Scams and Cybercrime Brief reported a 27.6% drop in scams compared with 2024 and an approximately 17.92% decrease in the total amount lost to scams within that same period.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: As Second Minister for Home Affairs Sim Ann pointed out during the Second Reading of the Criminal Law (Miscellaneous Offences) Bill last year, between 2020 and the first half of 2025, scams comprised approximately 60%, an outright majority of all crimes reported to the Police.

sections.label: Clause 7 account and service orders
sections.summary: Clause 7 introduces ADOs requiring service providers to disable specific accounts and SLOs restricting a user from using a scam enabling service.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Clause 7 introduces two new orders which law enforcement can issue to service providers, whether they are banks, payment services, telecommunications companies, or online service providers.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: An ADO requires service providers to disable specific accounts for anti-scam purposes, while a SLO, which builds on the provision set out in the facility restriction framework, mandate service providers, restrict a specific user from using a scam enabling service.

sections.label: Access under facility restriction framework
sections.summary: A Parliamentary reply noted that persons with accounts blocked under the facility restriction framework could still access basic banking services, receive payments and use physical bank branches.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: On this specific concern, a Parliamentary reply from September last year noted that persons whose accounts are blocked under the facility restriction framework could still have access to basic banking services, receive payments, such as their salary and government benefits, as well as withdraw and deposit money at physical bank branches.

sections.label: Overseas refund schemes and proposals
sections.summary: The passage cites UK and Australian refund schemes and repeats a call for an insurance scheme with a $500 consumer liability cap and a scam victim restitution fund.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: For instance, the United Kingdom (UK) has mandated that payment service providers refund banks up to £85,000 if a victim reported that they were subject to a scam unless the victim was grossly negligent or did not provide the payment service provider with all the information required for the investigations.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Australia is also planning to implement a similar scheme with a lower cap of AUD3,000, and with responsibility shared equally between the banks, telecommunications companies and social media platforms.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This also forced banks to step up their anti-scam measures by hitting them directly in the wallet.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Therefore, I would like to repeat the call contained in the Workers' Party's 2025 manifesto to have an insurance scheme to cover losses from scams with a consumer liability cap of up to $500 and to look into a scam victim restitution fund financed by recovered funds.

sections.label: Money laundering investigation sources
sections.summary: The report notes 82% of Singapore's money laundering investigations arose from Police reports by cyber-enabled fraud victims, versus 2% from financial and other intelligence sources.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The report notes that 82% of Singapore's money laundering investigations arose from Police reports filed by victims of cyber-enabled fraud, a stark contrast to the 2% from financial and other intelligence sources.

sections.label: COSMIC and elderly scam losses
sections.summary: COSMIC has helped close over 1,000 suspicious accounts and file reports for up to $1.6 billion, while elderly scam victims lost an average of about $42,347 in the first half of 2026.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Since its inception in 2024, the Collaborative Sharing of Money Laundering/TF Information and Cases (COSMIC), the Monetary Authority of Singapore's (MAS') customer information sharing platform aimed at curbing financial crime, has helped in closing over 1,000 suspicious customer accounts, with suspicious transaction reports filed for up to $1.6 billion in aggregate fund flows, according to a response to a Parliamentary Question I filed just last month.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Despite accounting for about 14.8% of victims in 2025, elderly scam victims lost an average of approximately $42,347 from scams during the first half of 2026, up from $35,374 over the same period in 2025, leaving them in a financially precarious state.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In one instance, over S$6.1 million was lost to scammers impersonating the Immigrations and Checkpoints Authority (ICA) or Chinese officials, while another case involved a scammer extorting around $600,000 by posing as Elon Musk.

sections.label: Scam losses fell
sections.summary: Losses fell to about $410.6 million in the first half of 2026, down some 18% from $500.2 million a year before.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Losses fell to about $410.6 million in the first half of 2026, down some 18% from $500.2 million lost in the same period a year before.

sections.label: Average loss per elderly victim
sections.summary: Police statistics show the average amount lost per elderly victim rose from about $35,000 in the first half of 2025 to over $42,000 in the same period this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Statistics from the police show that the average amount lost per elderly victim rose from about $35,000 in the first half of 2025, to over $42,000 in the same period this year.

sections.label: Account disabling order period
sections.summary: The passage states unpaid rent, missed installments and family strain, and asks the Minister how the 30-day period for an account disabling order was arrived at.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It can mean rent going unpaid, installments being missed and real strain on the family.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: So, my questions to the Minister are these: first, how was the 30-day period for an account disabling order arrived at?

sections.label: Lifting longer suspensions standards
sections.summary: The passage asks the Minister what service standards govern lifting longer suspensions once an innocent party is cleared and what records are needed to restore an account sooner.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: That is where the strain is felt most keenly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: So, I will ask the Minister what service standards govern the lifting of these longer suspensions once an innocent party is cleared and what records does that person have to have their account restored sooner?

sections.label: Police disrupt scam lines websites
sections.summary: In the first half of this year, Police disrupted tens of thousands of scam-related mobile lines, WhatsApp lines and malicious websites.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In the first half of this year alone, the Police disrupted tens of thousands of scam-related mobile lines, WhatsApp lines and malicious websites.

sections.label: Man charged buying work permit e-wallets
sections.summary: A young man was charged with buying e-wallets from work permit holders for around $50 each, through which nearly $10,000 in scam proceeds flowed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: A young man charged with buying e-wallets from work permit holders, paying them around $50 each, through which nearly $10,000 in scam proceeds flowed.

sections.label: CSOs get investigative arrest powers
sections.summary: CSOs established under a new section in the Police Force Act have investigative and arrest powers equivalent to police officers of the same grade.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The establishment of CSOs under a new section in the Police Force Act gives them investigative and arrest powers equivalent to those of police officers of the same grade.

sections.label: Bill measures, scam losses, concerns raised
sections.summary: The speaker says the Bill's measure includes freeing wrongly frozen innocents, accountability and oversight, and notes Singaporeans lost $913 million to scams in 2025 with median loss rising to $1,644.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The measure of this Bill will not only be how many syndicate accounts we freeze.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It will be how quickly we free the innocent ones we freeze by mistake, how transparently our new officers and our new automated system are held to account and whether residents who loses their money in the grey zone still finds a door open somewhere in Government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I hope the Minister can address the concerns I have raised on the lifting of orders on the manpower, the placement of CSOs  and on the oversight of automated decisions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: But Singaporeans still lost $913 million to scams in 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: And while there were fewer cases, the median loss increased from $1,389 to $1,644.

sections.label: Operation FRONTIER+ III arrests freezes
sections.summary: Between March and May this year, Operation FRONTIER+ III saw Singapore and nine other jurisdictions arrest over 3,000 people and freeze over $200 million in scam-linked funds, with Singapore's Anti-Scam Centre accounting for $35 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Between March and May this year, Operation FRONTIER+ III saw Singapore and nine other jurisdictions arrest more than 3,000 people and freeze more than $200 million in scam-linked funds across the region.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Singapore's own Anti-Scam Centre accounted for $35 million of that total.

sections.label: Selection, training, review, guiding principles
sections.summary: The speaker asks how officers will be selected, trained and supervised, suggests a statutory review after three to five years, supports the Bill, and sets out three guiding principles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: But I would also like to ask how these officers will be selected, trained and supervised, given the powers they will exercise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I would also suggest that the Government consider a statutory review of this Bill, perhaps after three to five years, to assess whether these powers remain proportionate and effective as scam tactics continue to evolve.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: When we close one channel, they will look for another.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I support this Bill because it allows us to go beyond targeting individual scammers and disrupt the wider infrastructure that enables scams.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: As we implement these stronger powers, three principles should guide us: speed in stopping scams; safeguards for innocent users; and accountability from Government and service providers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: If we can stop the money before it reaches the scammers, we would have protected not just someone's money, but often years of hard work and savings.

sections.label: ADO duration and appeal right
sections.summary: An ADO is kept at 30 days, extendable once and no further, while clause 8 gives a disabled account user a right of appeal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: An ADO will be kept at 30 days, extendable once and no further, while clause 8 gives the user of a disabled account a right of appeal.

sections.label: Protection from Scams Act restriction orders
sections.summary: The Protection from Scams Act lets Police issue restriction orders to banks, with 12 issued as of February 2026, and section 35 of the CPC has no maximum period, automatic review or duty to give reasons.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For instance, this House passed the Protection from Scams Act last year, which empowers the Police to step in and issue restriction orders to banks if there is reasonable belief that account holders will be making transfers to scammers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, such account holders are still permitted access to funds for essential daily living expenses and bills. n response to the Parliamentary Question from my hon friend, Mr Kenneth Tiong, MHA revealed that as of February 2026, only 12 restriction orders have been issued under the Protection from Scams Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Police approved withdrawals for daily expenses in 10 of the 12 cases, while no requests for withdrawal were made in the remaining two cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Unlike restriction orders and account disabling orders, section 35 of the CPC contains no maximum period, no automatic review and no duty to give reasons.

sections.label: Frozen bank accounts details sought
sections.summary: A Member asks for details on how many bank accounts were frozen, on what basis, under which statutory provision, and for how long, and asks for reassurance that an SLO will be levied sparingly and carefully.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: On a related note, Mr Speaker, I hope the Government can share more details about how many bank accounts have been frozen and on what basis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I understand that the Anti-Scam Command froze more than 15,000 accounts last year and more than 16,700 accounts were frozen in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Can the Senior Minister of State provide a breakdown of the number of bank accounts that have been frozen, including for non-scam related reasons.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In each of the past two years, under which statutory provision and the average and median duration that these accounts were frozen?

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Can the Senior Minister of State reassure the public that such an SLO will be levied sparingly and carefully.

sections.label: Businessman transferred $4.9 million
sections.summary: By the time the businessman realised what had happened, he had transferred at least $4.9 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
sentences.text: By the time the businessman realised what had happened, he had transferred at least $4.9 million.

sections.label: Scams cost victims $913.1 million
sections.summary: Scams cost victims in Singapore $913.1 million last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Scams cost victims in Singapore $913.1 million last year.

sections.label: ADO 30-day disablement and extension
sections.summary: ADOs will allow accounts suspected of facilitating scam-related offences to be disabled for up to 30 days, with one possible extension of up to another 30 days.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
sentences.text: ADOs will allow accounts suspected of facilitating scam-related offences to be disabled for up to 30 days, with one possible extension of up to another 30 days.

sections.label: Bill coverage and penalties
sections.summary: The Bill covers financial institutions, telcos and online services, with penalties up to $10 million for non-compliant designated online providers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In fact, the Bill's definition of service providers already covers financial institutions, telecommunications service providers and providers of online services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This Bill also provides for financial penalties of up to $10 million for each instance of non-compliance by designated online service providers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I would ask the Ministry to say more about how these powers will be used.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I would also ask whether the Government intends to set different duties or standards for the different types of service providers covered by the Bill, given that a bank, a telco and an online platform may see different parts of the same scam.

sections.label: Earlier action for seniors
sections.summary: Seniors had the highest average loss per scam victim last year at $37,053 each, so earlier action is needed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
sentences.text: And the earlier we can step in, the more victims we may be able to prevent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This is especially important for our seniors, who last year suffered the highest average loss per scam victim among all age groups, at $37,053 each.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
sentences.text: We need to act earlier, protect innocent users and make sure that everyone in the scam system plays a part in stopping scams.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Overall, I think that this Bill is a step in the right direction and I hope the Ministry will continue to strengthen our approach, especially in the areas of open data, protection for innocent users and shared responsibility.

sections.label: Accountability and victim compensation
sections.summary: The Bill raises maximum administrative penalties for non-compliant online providers to $10 million and targets money mules.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I stress the importance of greater accountability from digital platforms and service providers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This Bill strengthens the deterrence by increasing maximum administrative financial penalties for non-compliant online providers to $10 million, alongside targeted measures to crack down on money mules who surrender their credentials.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: First, the Government should establish a clear statutory victim compensation framework that holds financial institutions, telcos and digital platforms accountable when their anti-scam measures failed to protect customers.

sections.label: Standardised anti-scam rating system
sections.summary: MAS and IMDA should introduce a standardised public rating system assessing anti-scam performance of financial institutions, telcos and online platforms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Third, MAS and IMDA should introduce a standardised public rating system to regularly assess and publish the anti-scam performance of financial institutions, telcos and online platforms.

sections.label: Scam victim restitution fund
sections.summary: A dedicated scam victim restitution fund should be established.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Fifth, a dedicated scam victim restitution fund should be established.

sections.label: SLO and ADO restrictions
sections.summary: SLOs can restrict access to scam-enabling services for up to three years, while ADOs can restrict bank, payment, telephone and online accounts.

sentences.speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: SLOs can restrict access to scam-enabling services for up to three years, while ADOs can restrict the use of bank and payment accounts, telephone lines and online accounts.

sections.label: Proportionality and individual vulnerability
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister how proportionality and individual vulnerability will be considered when these powers are exercised.

sentences.speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Our implementation framework needs to be capable of recognising this possibility.

sentences.speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I therefore ask the Minister how proportionality and individual vulnerability will be considered when these powers are exercised.

sections.label: Variation of ADO
sections.summary: An ADO may be varied to permit particular transactions, subject to appropriate limits or conditions.

sentences.speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: An ADO may be varied to permit particular transactions, subject to appropriate limits or conditions.

sections.label: Assessing circumstances and essential services
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Senior Minister of State how such circumstances will be assessed and continued access to essential services addressed for vulnerable persons.

sentences.speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Could the Senior Minister of State elaborate on how such circumstances will be assessed and how continued access to essential services will be addressed for persons with particular vulnerabilities?

sections.label: SPF scam and cybercrime figures
sections.summary: SPF briefs state over 15,000 bank accounts were frozen and self-effected transfer scams rose to 80.8% in the first half of 2026.

sentences.speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: According to the Singapore Police Force's (SPF's) 2025 Scam and Cybercrime Brief, more than 15,000 bank accounts were frozen.

sentences.speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: According to SPF's 2026 Mid-Year Scam and Cybercrime Brief, scams involving self-effected transfers rose to 80.8% in the first half of 2026, up from 78.8% in the same period last year.

sections.label: Basic banking services definition
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether a similar principle could apply to anyone unable to obtain an account, and whether basic services can be defined.

sentences.speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Given that the facility restriction framework already preserves basic banking access, even for persons assessed to present mule-related risks, could a similar principle apply to any person who cannot obtain an account anywhere?

sentences.speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Regardless of which anti-scam or investigative mechanism causes the restriction, can we define the basic services that should remain available, such as receiving verified salary and Government payments, paying essential bills and reasonable access to money for daily expenses?

sections.label: Suspicion triggering consequential action
sections.summary: The Bill moves onto grounds where suspicion alone can trigger consequential action, ahead of traditional judicial thresholds of proof.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: But as we move further upstream to keep ahead of the scammers, we find ourselves moving ahead of the traditional thresholds of proof that normally apply in the judicial process.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: This Bill moves us onto grounds where suspicion alone can trigger consequential action and those consequences can be serious.

sections.label: Officer suspicion of scam use
sections.summary: An officer may act if he suspects or believes a service or account will be or has been used for a scam-related offence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: An officer may act where he suspects or has reason to believe that a service or an account will be or has been used to commit or facilitate a scam-related offence.

sections.label: Account disabled by association
sections.summary: An account can be disabled for transacting with a specific account or, for telephone or online accounts, communicating with the wrong person.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: An account can be disabled if it has carried out a transaction with a specific account or, in the case of a telephone or online account, simply having communicated with the wrong person.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: This is concerning because it is essentially the possibility of suspicion by association alone.

sections.label: Sections 9A and 9B powers
sections.summary: Sections 9A and 9B of the Protection from Scams Act let a bank, telco or platform act on its own initiative without a Police order.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: This, together with the new sections 9A and 9B of the Protection from Scams Act.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: It allows a bank, telco or platform to take action on its own initiative, without the Police having to issue an order against that specific account so long as its suspicions are drawn, even partly from information obtained from another order.

sections.label: Bank retaining suspected customer justification
sections.summary: A bank that chooses to retain a suspected customer must justify that decision in writing.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: If a bank chooses to retain a suspected customer, it has to justify that decision in writing.

sections.label: NSL as de facto blacklist
sections.summary: The passage asks what stops the NSL from becoming a unilateral and de facto blacklist for banks, telcos and platforms.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: What stops the NSL from becoming a unilateral and de facto blacklist for our banks, telcos and platforms?

sections.label: Cleared persons still refused service
sections.summary: The passage asks what stops service providers from continuing to refuse service to someone cleared and removed from the NSL.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: When someone is cleared of any suspicions of wrongdoing and removed from the NSL, what stops the service providers from still erring from the side of caution and continuing to exercise their business prerogative to continue to refuse service?

sections.label: Unaddressed questions and scant guardrails
sections.summary: The Bill does not address these uncomfortable questions, and there are scant guardrails against excessive action by service providers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: These are uncomfortable questions that the Bill does not address, Mr Speaker, and there are many more.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: It is clear there are scant guardrails in place against excessive action by service providers.

sections.label: New section 6G disclosure orders
sections.summary: New section 6G allows Police to issue DOs requiring service providers to disclose information about bank, payment, digital-token, telephone and online accounts.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: The new section 6G allows the Police to issue DOs requiring service providers to disclose information about bank, payment, digital-token, telephone and online accounts.

sections.label: Section 6B(2) account disabling
sections.summary: Section 6B(2) allows accounts meeting specified disabling conditions to be disabled.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: Section 6B(2) goes further by allowing accounts that meet specified disabling conditions to be disabled.

sections.label: Request for published aggregate indicators
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the Ministry will publish aggregate indicators on detection-to-disclosure and disabling times, false-positive and restoration rates, losses prevented, and scammer migration.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: More broadly, I hope the Ministry will publish aggregate indicators covering the time from detection to disclosure and disabling; false-positive and restoration rates; estimated losses prevented and evidence that scammers migrated to replacement accounts or services.

sections.label: Action before money transferred
sections.summary: For residents, what matters most is whether action can be taken before the money is transferred away, not how many orders are issued.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: For residents, what matters most is not how many orders are issued, but whether action can be taken before the money is transferred away.

sections.label: Scam cases and losses last year
sections.summary: Last year there were 37,308 scam cases, with losses totaling $913.1 million.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Last year alone, there were 37,308 scams cases, with losses totaling $913.1 million.

sections.label: SLO and ADO powers
sections.summary: A specified officer may issue an SLO for up to three years or an ADO for up to 30 days, extendable once to 60 days, on suspicion of scam use.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Under the new sections 6A and 6B, a specified officer may issue an SLO for up to three years, or an ADO for up to 30 days extendable once to 60 days, whenever he suspects or has reason to believe that a person will use, or an account has been used, to facilitate a scam.

sections.label: Reasonable suspicion threshold question
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether reasonable suspicion, a higher bar used elsewhere, would better justify exercising such power.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Might reasonable suspicion, the higher bar used elsewhere in our statute book, be a better threshold that justifies the exercise of such power?

sections.label: Reverse presumption for gain
sections.summary: The speaker supports criminalising account sales to scam syndicates but says the presumption of acting for any gain casts a wide net.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Next, the reverse presumption in the new sections 39GA to 39GC of the Miscellaneous Offences Act.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I support criminalising the sale of accounts to scam syndicates, but the presumption that a person acted "for any gain" casts a wide net.

sections.label: Victims transferring own money
sections.summary: SPF's February brief states 81.8% of last year's scam cases involved victims transferring their own money after being deceived.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The prevention gap: SPF's Annual Scam and Cybercrime Brief, published in February this year, tells us that 81.8% of last year's scam cases involved victims transferring their own money, having been deceived into doing so willingly.

sections.label: Digital payment token providers duties
sections.summary: The passage states it does not yet place duties on digital payment token providers, though cryptocurrency accounts for roughly a fifth of scam losses, some $182 million last year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Neither, as far as I understand, does it yet place duties on digital payment token providers, even though cryptocurrency now accounts for roughly a fifth of all scam losses – some $182 million last year.

sections.label: Penalties flow to state
sections.summary: Clause 21's financial penalties on non-compliant platforms are welcome but flow to the state, not the victim.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The redress gap: clause 21's financial penalties on non-compliant platforms are welcome.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: But they flow to the state, not the victim.

sections.label: Elderly scam victims losses
sections.summary: Those aged 65 and above were about 15% of scam victims, with average losses over $37,000 in 2025 and $42,000 in the first half of the year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: Last year, those aged 65 and above accounted for about 15% of scam victims.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: The average amount lost by an elderly victim was more than $37,000 in 2025, and rose to $42,000 in the first half of the year.

sections.label: Young adult scam cases
sections.summary: Last year, those aged 20 to 29 accounted for almost one in five scam cases.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: Last year, those aged 20 to 29 accounted for almost one in five scam cases.

sections.label: Online platforms used by scammers
sections.summary: Last year, scammers used online platforms to reach victims in more than 84% of all scam cases.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: Last year, online platforms were used by scammers to reach victims in around more than 84% of all scam cases.

sections.label: ADO duration and extension
sections.summary: Under the Bill, an ADO may last up to 30 days, with a further extension.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: Under the Bill, an ADO may last for up to 30 days, with a further extension.

sections.label: Young adult scam victims share
sections.summary: Nearly 20% of scam victims are between 20 and 29 years old.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: Nearly 20% of scam victims are between 20 and 29 years old.

sections.label: Online scam cases and penalties
sections.summary: Last year, more than 84% of scam cases started online, and digital platforms failing their responsibilities can face penalties up to $10 million.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: Last year, more than 84% of scam cases started online.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: Digital platforms that fail to fulfil their responsibilities can face penalties of up to $10 million.

sections.label: Expedited review for blocked accounts
sections.summary: The speaker suggests an expedited review process for those whose accounts are wrongly blocked and supports avenues for temporary funds.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: These powers are important, but I suggest an expedited review process for those who believe their accounts have been blocked incorrectly.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: I often receive appeals from my Fengshan residents who find themselves in difficult situations because they are unable to access their funds.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: Several Members of Parliament who spoke earlier offered suggestions which I support, including providing an avenue for victims to access temporary funds.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: True success is when scam content can be removed earlier, when fewer Singaporeans lose their hard-earned money, and when families no longer lose savings accumulated over a lifetime.

sections.label: Need for smarter prevention
sections.summary: The speaker says laws alone are not enough and calls for smarter prevention, targeted education, platform responsibility and faster intervention.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: But laws alone will not be enough, Mr Speaker, Sir.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: We need smarter prevention, more targeted education, greater responsibility from platforms and faster intervention.

sections.label: Distinguishing passive money mules
sections.summary: The speaker says the law should distinguish passive money mules from those who knowingly recruit account holders and conceal scam proceeds.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: At the same time, our law should distinguish between passive money mules and those who knowingly recruit other account holders, manage a network of accounts and professionally layer and conceal the scam proceeds.

sections.label: Residents unable to access accounts
sections.summary: At MPS in Geylang Serai, the speaker met residents unable to access existing bank accounts or open new ones due to scam-related transactions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: At my MPS in Geylang Serai, I have met residents who are unable to access their existing bank accounts or open new accounts due to scam-related transactions being performed on their accounts.

sections.label: Resident could not afford lawyer
sections.summary: A resident could not afford a lawyer to apply to Court for fund access precisely because his money was frozen.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: When I previously raised this issue in this House, I was told that an affected person could apply to Court for access to funds for basic living expenses.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: But one resident who came and see me with this problem could not even afford a lawyer, precisely because his money was frozen.

sections.label: Releasing salaries and payouts
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether verified salaries and Government payouts could be released for essential expenses where operationally safe.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: Where it is operationally safe, could verified salaries and Government payouts be released for essential expenses?

sections.label: Human review of automated directions
sections.summary: Asks whether automated directions get meaningful human review and whether flawed rules trigger proactive review of other affected cases.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: When an automated direction is challenged, will there be meaningful human review of the outcome, of the evidence?

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: If a flawed rule is discovered, will the authorities proactively review other cases affected by it?

sections.label: Verifying genuine officers
sections.summary: Asks how members of the public will verify that such an officer is genuine.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: How will members of public verify that such an officer is genuine?

sections.label: Restrictions for essential living expenses
sections.summary: States restrictions are calibrated to allow access to funds needed for essential living expenses where it is safe to do so.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: Second, restrictions that are calibrated to allow persons to access funds needed for essential living expenses where it is safe to do so.

sections.label: Crypto tracing recoveries and ADOs
sections.summary: States 2025 crypto-tracing recoveries and interventions, and that an ADO may be issued on suspicion an account is used for scam-related offences.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
sentences.text: In 2025, the crypto-tracing teams successfully recovered $22.8 million worth of virtual assets across 1,800 cases and helped prevent $8.8 million in losses through 360 victim interventions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
sentences.text: An ADO may be issued if there is suspicion or reason to believe that an account has been or will be used preparatory to, or in furtherance of, scam-related offences.

sections.label: Thirty-day account disablement period
sections.summary: States the 30-day period is operationally necessary for scam disruption and ADOs can require disabling the specified account for up to 30 days.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
sentences.text: The period of 30 days is operationally necessary for scam disruption.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
sentences.text: To be clear, ADOs can impose a requirement to disable the specified account for up to 30 days.

sections.label: Victim's savings transferred to scammer
sections.summary: States the victim had transferred about S$128,000 in cryptocurrency and was near transferring another S$64,000, with about S$2 million lost daily.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
sentences.text: By the time officers engaged the victim, the victim had already transferred 80 percent, eight zero, 80 percent of his life savings, or approximately S$128,000 in cryptocurrency to the scammer.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
sentences.text: He was also on the verge of transferring another S$64,000 of borrowed funds to the scammer.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
sentences.text: On average, about S$2 million was lost to scams every day, in the first half of this year.

sections.label: Mule restrictions and durations
sections.summary: First-time mules generally face one year of restrictions, with longer durations for repeat offenders or sustained scam risk.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
sentences.text: First-time mules will generally face one year of restrictions, while longer durations may be warranted for repeat offenders or those assessed to pose a sustained scam risk.

sections.label: Banking restrictions under SLOs
sections.summary: Restricted individuals may still transact over the counter; only self-service banking like Internet, mobile and ATM services is restricted.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
sentences.text: Ms He Ting Ru asked about the banking restrictions imposed on individuals whose accounts have been restricted under the Facility Restricted Framework.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
sentences.text: I wish to reassure the House that we will not prevent individuals from accessing funds that they genuinely need for daily living.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
sentences.text: Individuals subject to banking restrictions under SLOs may still transact personally at the bank, over the counter.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
sentences.text: We will only restrict access to self-service banking services, like Internet banking, mobile banking or ATM services, which are more prone to being exploited for scams.

sections.label: Limited Purpose Banking Accounts offered
sections.summary: In 2025, major retail banks offered close to 8,300 Limited Purpose Banking Accounts.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
sentences.text: In 2025, major retail banks offered close to 8,300 Limited Purpose Banking Accounts (LPBAs).

sections.label: Singpass restrictions target scam-prone services
sections.summary: Singpass restrictions target higher-risk services like opening a bank account, while voting, healthcare and CPF matters remain fully accessible.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
sentences.text: The Singpass restrictions will only be targeted at services that are at higher risk of being exploited for scams, such as opening a bank account.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
sentences.text: Services listed by the Member, namely voting, healthcare and CPF matters, remain fully accessible.

sections.label: Presumption applies to any gain
sections.summary: The Government's view is that the presumption should apply so long as there is gain, no matter how small.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
sentences.text: The Government's view is that the presumption should apply so long as there is gain, no matter how small.

sections.label: Website blocking reconsideration requests
sections.summary: Out of over 70,000 website blocking directions issued in 2026, the Police received only six reconsideration requests.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
sentences.text: Out of over 70,000 website blocking directions issued in 2026, the Police only received six reconsideration requests.

sections.label: ScamShield AI classifier development
sections.summary: The AI powered classifier for ScamShield was developed in the first quarter of 2024 and operationalised a few months later.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
sentences.text: For example, the AI powered classifier for ScamShield was developed in the first quarter of 2024 and operationalised a few months later.

sections.label: Appeal review timeframe
sections.summary: Review of appeals can be expected to be completed within seven days for straightforward and unambiguous appeals, though time taken depends on nature and complexity.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
sentences.text: While the time taken for appeals depend on the nature and complexity of the appeals, the review can be expected to be completed within seven days for straightforward and unambiguous appeals.

sections.label: Financial penalty decision factors
sections.summary: The decision to issue a financial penalty or direct rectification, and the penalty quantum, will depend on a variety of factors.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
sentences.text: The decision to issue a financial penalty or direct the platform to rectify the non-compliance, as well as the quantum of financial penalty to impose, will depend on a variety of factors.

sections.label: CSO recruitment sources
sections.summary: CSOs may be recruited directly from the market or seconded from other public agencies such as the Cyber Security Agency.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
sentences.text: CSOs may be recruited directly from the market, or may be seconded from other public agencies, such as the Cyber Security Agency.

sections.label: Account freeze duration and safeguards
sections.summary: Account freeze duration varies by case, and the Criminal Procedure Code requires a police report of seizure to the Court once property is no longer required or within one year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
sentences.text: The duration for which an account is frozen varies from case to case depending on the duration required for investigations or court proceedings.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
sentences.text: As a safeguard, the Criminal Procedure Code requires that the police make a report of seizure to the relevant Court once the property is no longer required for investigations or court proceedings, or within one year after the date of seizure, whichever is earlier.

sections.label: ADO lower threshold rationale
sections.summary: ADOs can be exercised at a lower threshold to allow the police to keep pace with the speed at which scam syndicates create and replace accounts.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
sentences.text: On the other hand, ADOs can be exercised at a lower threshold to allow the police to keep pace with the speed at which scam syndicates can create and replace accounts.

sections.label: Anti-scam outreach and exercise
sections.summary: Scam messages are injected into getai performances and youth outreach, and a National Simulated Scams Exercise used robo-callers between March and August.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
sentences.text: We even inject scam messages into getai performances and we have similar outreach efforts for other groups such as our youths.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
sentences.text: We also recently concluded the National Simulated Scams Exercise held between March and August this year, which involved the use of robo-callers to simulate calls from scammers to strengthen participants’ anti-scam resilience.

sections.label: FRONTIER+ jurisdictions
sections.summary: FRONTIER+ now covers 15 jurisdictions, with the United States and the Philippines joining earlier this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: FRONTIER+ now covers 15 jurisdictions, with the United States and the Philippines joining earlier this year.

sections.label: Bill tools against scams
sections.summary: The Government will work with industry to disrupt scams, and the Bill gives tools for swifter, more proactive action against scams.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: The Government will indeed continue to work closely with industry to disrupt scams quickly and with precision.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: But as I mentioned earlier, about $2 million of our citizens' hard-earned money is still lost to scammers every single day.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: This Bill gives the Government the tools to enable swifter, more proactive and decisive action against scams.

sections.label: Support sought for Bill
sections.summary: The speaker seeks Members' support on the Bill to fight scams and better protect people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: When we do, scammers have fewer places to hide, fewer tools to exploit and fewer opportunities to cause harm.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: I seek Members' support on this Bill, to move decisively and reflect this House's commitment to fight scams and better protect our people.

sections.label: Recovered amounts versus losses
sections.summary: One factor is that amounts recovered are only a fraction of the overall amounts lost.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: One factor indeed is that amounts recovered are but a fraction of the overall amounts lost.

sections.label: Moral hazard and restitution fund
sections.summary: A baseline repayment amount could lower public vigilance, and recovered funds do not stay in the Government's coffers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: The other question here is also about moral hazard.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: If we establish that there is a certain baseline amount – I think the Member has asked this question before, whether we are able to have a certain minimum repayment amount for every scam victim – the overall awareness and vigilance of members of the public may fall, because they will get the sense that buying the next concert ticket, they have certain protections, up to a certain amount for scam protection.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: I think there are many questions that we need to deal with in terms of how we can operationalise such a restitution fund.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: But on the Member's other point about some of the funds that we have recovered which have gone back to the Consolidated Fund for the Government, I want to put out the point that these monies do not go back to the Government's coffers and just stay there.
